answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a deposit and build a work history before transacting. Like a jetty that only admits proven boats, the network gives new identities a narrow horizon of low-value tasks and widens permissions only after completed work. Faking reputation is ivory-tower expensive: a credible history takes weeks of real computation, and one detected fraud burns both stake and history. An attacker needing a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits plus a thousand histories, so the attack costs far more than the fraud could return.
